terms.definition: Identity and Access Management — AWS's central service for controlling who can do what in your account. Every API call passes through IAM.
terms.example: Creating a user, group, or role in the AWS console is an IAM operation.

terms.definition: An IAM entity that can make API calls: root user, IAM user, IAM group (indirectly), or IAM role.
terms.example: An EC2 instance using a role is a principal when calling S3.

terms.definition: Proving who you are. Established by credential type: password, access key, STS token, or federated assertion.
terms.example: Entering your username and password in the console is authentication.

terms.definition: Determining if an authenticated caller is permitted to perform an action on a resource. Established by IAM policy evaluation.
terms.example: The three-step rule (deny → allow → implicit deny) governs authorization.

terms.definition: The ability to answer 'who did what, when, and from where.' Established by AWS CloudTrail.
terms.example: CloudTrail logs show that alice-analyst called s3:GetObject at 10:43 AM from IP 1.2.3.4.

terms.definition: The account creator's intrinsic identity, unconstrained by any policy. Has 100% blast radius if compromised. Cannot be deleted.
terms.example: You use the root user to close an AWS account — never for daily work.

terms.definition: A long-lived identity with username, password, and optional access keys. One per human. Credentials are managed in IAM.
terms.example: alice-analyst is an IAM user who signs into the console with MFA.

terms.definition: A permission management container — NOT an identity. Holds IAM users and a set of policies. Groups cannot be principals in resource-based policies.
terms.example: DataAnalystGroup holds all analysts and grants them s3:GetObject on the videos bucket.

terms.definition: A temporary identity assumed via AWS STS. Issues short-lived credentials that expire automatically. Used for workloads and cross-account access.
terms.example: An EC2 instance in Account B assumes DataAnalystRole in Account A to read encrypted videos.

terms.definition: A policy attached to an IAM principal (user, group, role). Answers 'what can this principal do?' The Principal element is implicit.
terms.example: Attaching an S3 read policy to the DataAnalystRole is an identity-based policy.

terms.definition: A policy attached to an AWS resource (S3 bucket, KMS key, etc.). Answers 'who can do what to this resource?' Requires an explicit Principal element.
terms.example: An S3 bucket policy that denies DeleteObject to DataAnalystRole is a resource-based policy.

terms.definition: Amazon Resource Name — the globally unique address of every AWS resource. Format: arn:aws:service:region:account-id:resource
terms.example: arn:aws:s3:::acme-reports/quarterly/* — an S3 ARN (no region or account-id, unique to S3).

terms.definition: Granting the smallest action scope and resource scope that satisfies the functional requirement — nothing more.
terms.example: Granting s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::bucket/prefix/* instead of s3:* on *.

terms.definition: AWS Security Token Service — issues short-lived, temporary credentials when a role is assumed. The bridge in cross-account access.
terms.example: An EC2 instance calls sts:AssumeRole to receive temporary credentials valid for 1 hour.

terms.definition: A Deny statement in any IAM policy. Overrides any Allow anywhere — in any policy type, same account or cross-account. Cannot be overridden.
terms.example: A bucket policy with Deny on s3:DeleteObject for DataAnalystRole blocks deletion even if the role's identity-based policy allows it.

terms.definition: AWS's default behavior — if no explicit Allow applies, access is denied. AWS is deny-by-default.
terms.example: A brand new IAM user with no policies attached cannot do anything — implicit deny applies to all actions.

terms.definition: An advanced feature that caps the maximum permissions an IAM user or role can have. Acts as a ceiling — the effective permissions are the intersection of the boundary and the attached policies.
terms.example: Attaching a boundary to bob-developer ensures he cannot grant himself more than developer-scope permissions.

terms.definition: A key-value test in an IAM policy that constrains when the policy applies, based on request context. Examples: source IP, MFA presence, MFA age, time of day.
terms.example: Condition: NumericLessThan: aws:MultiFactorAuthAge: 900 requires MFA issued within 15 minutes.

terms.definition: A boolean condition key that is true if the session was authenticated with MFA at session start. Remains true for the entire session lifetime.
terms.example: Used for read-only operations: if MultiFactorAuthPresent is true, the user authenticated with MFA at some point today.

terms.definition: A numeric condition key (seconds) representing elapsed time since MFA credential was issued. Increases as the session ages. Use NumericLessThan to enforce recency.
terms.example: NumericLessThan: aws:MultiFactorAuthAge: 900 forces re-authentication with MFA if more than 15 minutes have passed.

terms.definition: When a principal in one AWS account accesses a resource in a different AWS account. Requires explicit Allow on both sides. The two-pronged rule applies for KMS.
terms.example: EC2 in Account B assumes a role in Account A to read KMS-encrypted S3 objects.

terms.definition: A container for an IAM role that can be attached to an EC2 instance. The instance uses the role's temporary credentials automatically via the instance metadata service.
terms.example: TranscoderRole is attached as an instance profile to EC2 instances in Account B.

terms.definition: For cross-account KMS decryption, both the IAM role policy AND the KMS key resource policy must independently permit kms:Decrypt. One side alone is insufficient.
terms.example: DataAnalystRole must allow kms:Decrypt AND the KMS key policy must also allow DataAnalystRole to decrypt.

terms.definition: CloudTrail logging for data-plane API operations on S3 objects (GetObject, PutObject, DeleteObject). Not enabled by default — must be configured. Required for audit compliance.
terms.example: Enabling S3 data events on the acme-videos bucket captures every GetObject call with caller identity and source IP.

terms.definition: Service Control Policy — an AWS Organizations feature that sets maximum permission boundaries for accounts or OUs within an organization. Applies even to the root user of member accounts.
terms.example: An SCP that denies s3:DeleteBucket applies to all principals in the account, overriding any Allow.
